overall_assessment:
Result: not accepted pending TQA-CP36G-01. The frozen source shows no observed implementation, DI-parity, routing, retry, or test-control bypass defect. Its local evidence is strong, but the grant-parser test matrix does not yet fully protect the stated provider contract.

| Five-question audit | Assessment | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Product and contract alignment | Mostly aligned | Production Meta parsing, bounded verification, safe error mapping, CAS/lease behavior, and exact ownership checks are exercised across unit, real-PostgreSQL E2E, and a production-adapter bridge. |
| Pass-the-test or brittle-shortcut risk | No bypass observed | No focused/skipped tests, retries, sleeps, provider-URL following, generic mock fallback, or test-only production route was found in the bounded audit surface. Browser execution serves a fresh built bundle; API tests use the production provider token where the real adapter boundary matters. |
| Assertion efficacy | Strong but incomplete | Assertions cover call count, fixed Graph host, bounded pagination, safe public errors, durable state, lease release, no version bump on convergence, and unchanged state after failure. Genuine RED evidence preceded the parser additions. |
| Assertion efficiency | Acceptable within local evidence | Verification is bounded to one grant check plus at most two number pages, each request has a timeout, and focused unit fixtures prove malformed boundary inputs without needless end-to-end duplication. No capacity or external-provider latency claim is established. |
| Positive, negative, and failure coverage | Insufficient for acceptance | Malformed scopes, granular scopes, and target IDs are covered, but required scalar-field failures and legitimate omission cases remain unprotected. |

| Test layer / environment | Status | Audit conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Meta client unit tests | Present | 47 client tests cover pagination, malformed nested structures, full WABA membership, and typed failure behavior. |
| API unit suite | Passed | 167 tests in the recorded all2 run. |
| Real PostgreSQL API E2E | Passed | 288 tests exercise persistence, attempt convergence, ownership, lease, and error-state invariants. |
| Web unit suite | Passed | 28 tests in the recorded all2 run. |
| Built browser suite | Passed | 47 tests against the fresh served bundle; the changed invite assertions wait for the exact BFF request and status. |
| External Meta/operator runtime | Pending by design | Local proof does not establish provider behavior, corrected-runtime recovery, or human receipt operations. |

| Boundary / DI / bypass matrix | Result |
|---|---|
| Production binding | MetaHttpClient is bound to the production META_CLIENT token. |
| Test seam | Tests override that exact token; the E2E bridge invokes the real MetaHttpClient verification method and its real typed error class. |
| Failure containment | Expected provider-boundary failures become the fixed safe 503 response; generic injected errors are not falsely reclassified as provider failures. |
| Control-flow limits | Exact numeric epoch handling, two-page cap, cursor validation, fixed host, redirect rejection, and no provider pagination URL following are asserted. |
| Test-control hygiene | No skip, only, retry, or timing-wait bypass was found in the bounded source and relevant runner configuration. |

| Decision / module adherence | Status |
|---|---|
| D-01 BU canonical identity | Supported by exact owner and identity assertions. |
| D-02 official provider verification | Supported locally; external-provider confirmation remains pending. |
| D-03 scoped attempts, generation, epoch, and lease | Supported by real-PostgreSQL failure and convergence assertions. |

Residual uncertainty: the audit did not claim global unexpected-error log redaction, external-provider behavior, or operator/runtime completion. Those are distinct from the local test-quality finding.
recommended_path: Keep the checkpoint pending. Add direct MetaHttpClient tests for: a missing debug data object; non-string app_id; non-boolean is_valid; a valid grant with scopes omitted but required granular scopes present; and a valid irrelevant granular entry with target_ids omitted. Each malformed case should assert the typed failure and exactly one fetch; each valid-omission case should assert successful bounded verification. Then create a fresh source freeze, run the canonical full all suite, repeat this fresh test-quality audit, and send the resulting package to the separate final-review gate. No production behavior change is indicated by this finding.

findings.title: Grant-shape tests omit required scalar and legitimate-omission cases
findings.rationale: The parser in api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.ts rejects a missing or malformed debug-grant root, app_id, and is_valid, while intentionally allowing omitted optional scopes, granular_scopes, and target_ids. The frozen tests cover malformed scopes, granular_scopes, and target_ids, but do not directly cover missing data, malformed app_id, malformed is_valid, or valid omission of scopes with required granular scope authorization. A regression could therefore reject a legitimate provider grant or weaken scalar validation without failing the current focused matrix. This is a boundary-contract coverage gap, not an observed production behavior defect.
findings.suggested_action: Extend the Meta client table tests with the missing negative scalar cases and positive optional-field omission cases. Assert typed error identity and one fetch for malformed debug responses, and successful bounded verification for valid omission variants; then rerun the canonical full suite and fresh audit.
